title: The Weight of Abstract Nouns
text:
Abstract nouns such as justice, integrity and resilience name ideas rather than physical objects, yet they shape how people reason about the world. Scholars note that these words often carry a degree of ambiguity, since their meanings shift according to context and culture. A writer who uses them carelessly may leave readers uncertain about what is actually being claimed.

For this reason, careful writers tend to define such terms explicitly or anchor them in concrete examples. Doing so allows an argument to remain precise without sacrificing the breadth that abstract language provides. The skill lies in balancing generality with clarity, so that the reader can follow the reasoning from principle to application.

questions.text: According to the passage, what do abstract nouns name?
According to the passage, what can careful writers do to make abstract terms clearer?
options: Define them explicitly or use concrete examples
Avoid them completely in every text
Use them only in technical reports

questions.text: What does the passage imply about the meaning of abstract nouns?
options: Their meaning can depend on context and culture
Their meaning is fixed and identical everywhere
Their meaning is easy to determine without context
Their meaning matters only in scientific writing

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of good writing?
options: Good writing balances general ideas with clarity
Good writing should use only the most abstract language
Good writing avoids any discussion of principles
Good writing depends mainly on the length of the text

in a clear and direct way, without leaving anything implied
the wide range or scope of something

paragraph_translations: Substantivos abstratos, como justiça, integridade e resiliência, nomeiam ideias e não objetos físicos, mas moldam a forma como as pessoas raciocinam sobre o mundo. Estudiosos observam que essas palavras costumam carregar certa ambiguidade, já que seus significados mudam conforme o contexto e a cultura. Um escritor que as usa sem cuidado pode deixar o leitor incerto sobre o que está de fato sendo afirmado.

Por isso, escritores cuidadosos tendem a definir tais termos explicitamente ou a ancorá-los em exemplos concretos. Assim, o argumento permanece preciso sem abrir mão da amplitude que a linguagem abstrata oferece. A habilidade está em equilibrar generalidade e clareza, para que o leitor acompanhe o raciocínio do princípio até a aplicação.
